steps.content: [Workstation]
[Chat Message 2]
[Workstation]
A notification pops up, and for a moment Tracy thinks it might be something important. It's just idle office gossip. Expressionless, she closes it and opens another chat window.
[Chat Message 3]
[Workstation]
Evie has been standing behind Tracy long enough to lose count of how many times she's said her name. Tracy hasn't registered a single one.
At last, as Tracy clicks toward another Phanuel clip, Evie gives her shoulder a gentle tap.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Oh. Hey, Evie. What's up?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: The team lead had me forward you some files. It's leftover work from those colleagues who went on leave and stopped showing up.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Okay.
Tracy answers briskly and turns straight back to her screen.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I sent them this morning, actually. You never replied to my message. And I asked if you wanted to grab lunch, but you didn't show. I just wanted to check... are you doing okay?

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Me? I'm doing better than ever, seriously!
Evie opens her mouth to speak, then hesitates, her gaze drifting over Tracy's desk, now swallowed whole by pink Phanuel merchandise.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: If you've got a minute, maybe we could grab coffee downstairs? Just a quick break.
Tracy scrolls through the fan group chat, offering a distracted response without lifting her eyes from the screen.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Moonbucks? You go ahead. I'm swamped. Besides, that place is for actual employees with real salaries like you. My contractor pay is barely enough to scrape by... Oh, by the way, do you have your phone with you?
Something new flashes across her screen, and she suddenly grabs Evie's arm.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Y-yeah, I have it. Why?

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Phanuel's concert tickets are dropping early. I'm sending you the link right now, and my login. Front row, Section A. I need backup. Can't risk missing this on my own.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Of course. I mean, I'll try. Just don't count on my clicking speed...
Evie opens the link Tracy forwarded, her words faltering as she reads.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Wait. This is how much? Tracy, I could see Mimi-meow perform for a solid week for this kind of money!

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Mimi-meow? Seriously? You're comparing her to Phanuel? She's an underground idol with only a few thousand fans. I bet most people have never even heard of her...

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Tracy, that's kind of harsh...

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: You brought her up first... Do you even know? Phanuel dropped a single and hit ten thousand comments in an hour. She's got luxury brands fighting over her. Five major magazine covers, all in her debut year. She changes her hair, and it trends. How is she even in the same category as an underground idol?
Tracy points to the magazine on her desk.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Look, just one single page of Phanuel costs me a few hundred extra on top of the magazine price. Monica's in here too, and she used to be everywhere. Even she's old news now. So yeah, no offense, but Mimi-meow...

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: You know what, forget it. You wouldn't get it. Mimi-meow's whole crowd fits in a tiny venue. Go twice, and she probably knows your name. It's barely different from just texting her yourself.

Evie stares at Tracy in disbelief. This Tracy—tossing out fandom jargon with practiced ease, downplaying her idol without a second thought—is not quite the same person who once screamed and giggled beside her in the break room.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: You're right. I don't get it! I don't get how someone who used to count every coin before buying coffee is suddenly burning money like this! I never wanted to compete with you, Tracy. I just thought we were stepping away from the stress for a minute. Sharing the things that made us happy!
The sudden spike in volume draws stares from around the office.
[Workstation]
The weight of those stares presses in on Evie from all sides. Out of the corner of her eye, she tracks the office group chat exploding on Tracy's monitor, unread messages stacking up fast.
"Lol what's the tea? Rival stans throwing hands? Someone grab popcorn."
"Can I please change seats? I never want to hear 'Phanuel' again. I was actually a casual fan, but honestly? Her fans are the worst..."
"Is that a full-time employee arguing...? Don't tell me I got stuck with overtime last time because she was off stanning her idol."

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I do my work. I've always done my job. This is... just a hobby to unwind. It doesn't affect anything...
Evie starts to defend herself, but around the workstation, the onlookers duck their heads one by one and turn away. Online, however, the mockery and venom only intensify.
"Phanuel, yeah, I know her. Wasn't she just exposed for plagiarism? Says a lot about her fans, honestly."
"Never seen either of them work this hard. Shame they can't put that energy into anything useful..."
"Bet they don't treat their parents half as well as they treat their precious idol."

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: You've all got the wrong idea. I don't even go to that many shows... I'll be here this week, overtime, same as all of you...

No, that's not how it is. Not what any of you think. Whether it's Phanuel or Mimi-Meow, we gave because we wanted to, and it made us happy. We never hurt anyone... But the words never make it out of Evie's mouth.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Why are you explaining yourself? What, you're embarrassed now? Of being a fan? Or are you embarrassed of being my friend?
Tracy stares at her with hollow eyes.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: You're the one who told me to get into this.
Evie tries to speak, but the sight of Tracy's hollow, crooked smile chokes the words right out of her. This isn't the friend she knew.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: So are you helping me or not? Come on. It starts in ten minutes. They'll sell out in seconds... This is her first concert. Who knows when she'll do another one? If I miss this, I might never get another shot. Just tell me now if you're out. I need to hire a proxy buyer before it's too late...

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: And if none of us gets it, I'll have to go through scalpers... With Phanuel's popularity, front section scalped tickets are going to be insane. My credit card won't handle it... Right, Evie, you make more than me. Your limit must be higher. Your family's got money, right? Can I borrow some from you?
Her grip on Evie's wrist is crushing. She wrenches and twists, fighting with everything she has, until she finally pulls away.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I'm sorry. I don't think... I can't help you with this.
Clutching the red mark Tracy left on her wrist, she flees. Tracy stays by her desk, surrounded by her Phanuel shrine, casting a condescending gaze over the "outsiders" around her.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: What? Any of you want to help?
The crowd of onlookers ducks back behind their monitors, heads vanishing one by one.
[Chat Message 5]
[Late-Night Apartment]
In the deepest corner of Evie's closet, orange LED strips encircle a tiny shrine. Every underground live ticket she's ever bought, every Mimi-meow handshake pass, is tucked inside with care.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Did I mess up? Should I have never told Tracy to get into stanning?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: She's so different now. That's not the Tracy I know anymore...
Evie hugs her Mimi-meow plushie tight and curls into a ball.
This is her own tiny corner of the world. Whenever her father's scolding or her mother's sighs become too heavy to bear, she escapes here and pours her heart out to Mimi-meow.

She's told Mimi-meow everything: how she ended up at this suffocating corporation under the crushing weight of her family's expectations, how she met her very first friend, Tracy... all of it, right here.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I know those things she said... the rankings, the comparisons... she didn't mean them. That's just the space she's in now. Big fandoms run on numbers, on proving your idol is the best. It's just how it is.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I don't think I'm even upset about what she said about Mimi-meow...

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: It's just... I've been watching Phanuel slowly become the only thing that matters to her. Work doesn't matter. Life doesn't matter. Me, and even herself... none of it. It's like nothing registers anymore.
The Mimi-meow fan club page glows on Evie's phone. Her finger wavers above the exit button, frozen in hesitation.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Mimi-meow... am I going to end up like that too?
As if sensing her turmoil, her phone suddenly vibrates. Evie jolts, fumbling to open the notification.
Notification: Your starred account, Mimi-meow, just posted!

<color=#fb9259>Mimi-meow:</color> Today's event is all wrapped up! Thank you to everyone who came out and showed your support. And to those who couldn't make it, I know you're out there fighting your own battles right now.
<color=#fb9259>Mimi-meow:</color> Keep going. You've got this! Even when you can't see me, I'm cheering for you just as hard as you cheer for me! Let's keep walking this road together, okay?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Trust... walking together...
Evie seems to have found her answer.
